Confirmed: commit `5be3447` is an ancestor of the fix commit, and it's the point where the loop condition changed from `offsets.get(i) < position` to `offsets.get(i) <= position`, while `pageNum` still started at `0`. That combination causes an off-by-one overcounting of pages whenever `position` exactly equals a page-offset boundary. The later fix (`16abeae`) doesn't touch the loop condition — it compensates by changing the initial value from `0` to `-1`, which cancels out the extra increment introduced by the `<=` comparison.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 5be3447e77d228b4db8755bfdbcdb0844a756625

## Reasoning
(1) I ran `git log -p -L` over the `getPageNumberFor` method's line range to see its full evolution. This showed the method being refactored/rewritten across several commits (`ca07a40`, `ed189b8`, `75b7a71`, `a16d27f`, `5be3447`, `680c485`) leading up to the fix.

(2) In commit `5be3447e77d228b4db8755bfdbcdb0844a756625`, the pagination-counting loop was rewritten. Critically, the loop's exit condition changed from `offsets.get(i) < position` to `offsets.get(i) <= position`, while `int pageNum = 0;` was left unchanged (and remained unchanged in every subsequent commit until the fix). With `<=`, whenever `position` exactly matches an offset value, `pageNum` gets incremented one extra time compared to the original semantics, producing an off-by-one page number.

(3) The fix commit `16abeae` only changes `int pageNum = 0;` to `int pageNum = -1;` — it does not touch the `<=` condition. This is the classic pattern of compensating for an off-by-one introduced elsewhere: shifting the starting value down by one exactly offsets the extra increment caused by using `<=` instead of `<`. I verified `5be3447` is an ancestor of `16abeae` and that no other commit in between altered either the loop condition or the initial `pageNum` value, confirming `5be3447` as the sole point where the two became inconsistent and the bug was introduced.

I'm reasonably confident in this identification since the fix directly reverses the numeric effect of this one specific line changed in `5be3447`, and no intervening commit touched either related line.
